attributes.body_ja:
助動詞（じょどうし）の「そうだ」には、主（おも）に二（ふた）つの使（つか）い方（かた）があります。

１．伝聞（でんぶん） - 他（ほか）の人（ひと）から聞（き）いたことを伝（つた）える。

２．様態（ようたい） - 見（み）てわかる物事（ものごと）の様子（ようす）を表（あらわ）す。

ここでは、伝聞（でんぶん）の使（つか）い方（かた）を学（まな）びましょう（様態（ようたい）の使（つか）い方（かた）は別（べつ）のレッスンで扱（あつか）います）。伝聞（でんぶん）の「そうだ」または「そうです」は、他人（たにん）やどこかの情報源（じょうほうげん）から聞（き）いたことを、ほかの誰（だれ）かに伝（つた）えるときに使（つか）います。これは、動詞（どうし）やイ形容詞（けいようし）の普通形（ふつうけい）、または「だ」を付（つ）けた名詞（めいし）やナ形容詞（けいようし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）います。

「そうだ」には、話（はな）し手（て）がその情報（じょうほう）を１００（ひゃく）％（パーセント）確（たし）かだとは思（おも）っていないニュアンスがあるため、「ようだ」などの表現（ひょうげん）よりも、自信（じしん）がないときに使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

聞（き）いた話（はなし）を伝（つた）える伝聞（でんぶん）の「そうだ」と、目（め）で見（み）て判断（はんだん）する様態（ようたい）の「そうだ」には、活用（かつよう）に以下（いか）の違（ちが）いがあります。

動詞（どうし） -

降（ふ）るそうだ：辞書形（じしょけい） ＋ そうだ → 伝聞（でんぶん）

降（ふ）りそうだ：連用形（れんようけい） ＋ そうだ → 様態（ようたい）

イ形容詞（けいようし） -

寒（さむ）いそうだ：辞書形（じしょけい） ＋ そうだ → 伝聞（でんぶん）

寒（さむ）そうだ：「い」を取（と）った語幹（ごかん） ＋ そうだ → 様態（ようたい）

名詞（めいし）とナ形容詞（けいようし） -

綺麗（きれい）だそうだ：「だ」＋ そうだ → 伝聞（でんぶん）

綺麗（きれい）そうだ：「だ」を取（と）った語幹（ごかん） ＋ そうだ → 様態（ようたい）
attributes.body:
The auxiliary verb そうだ has two primary functions in Japanese. It can convey one of the following things:

Hearsay: 伝聞（でんぶん） - Highlighting things that have been heard from other people.

Appearance: 様態（ようたい） - Highlighting the way that things 'appear', or 'seem'.

The appearance nuance is covered in another lesson, so we will focus on hearsay in this grammar point. When used to repeat statements that have been heard from other people/sources, そうだ (or そうです) will be paired with the plain form of a verb or い-Adjective, or a noun/な-Adjective followed by だ.

そうだ always implies that the speaker is not 100% certain about the validity of the information that they are conveying. Due to this, it does not sound as confident as other expressions, like ようだ.

Caution

In order to avoid confusion between the そうだ that is used for repeating information, and the そうだ that is used for making observations, the following differences will need to be memorized.

Verbs -

降（ふ）るそうだ - Unaltered verb, そうだ that is repeating information.

降（ふ）りそうだ - Conjunctive form, そうだ that is used for making observations.

い-Adjectives -

寒（さむ）いそうだ - Unaltered adjective, そうだ that is repeating information.

寒（さむ）そうだ - い removed, そうだ that is used for making observations.

Nouns and な-Adjectives -

綺麗（きれい）だそうだ - だ is used before そうだ. This is repeating information.

綺麗（きれい）そうだ - No だ between the な-Adjective and そうだ. This is making an observation.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar
[AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: そうだ vs. らしい [video]
そうだ: Judgments Based on Other People’s Information

attributes.body: Both forms express observations similar to 'seems' or 'appears', but differ in nuance. そうだ is based on sensory clues, e.g. 雨が降りそうだ ('It looks like it'll rain.', because the sky is dark and the air is damp). ようだ is based on more concrete information or experience, e.g. 雨が降るようだ ('It seems it'll rain.' because people are carrying umbrellas, or the weather report said so).

first_relatable.title: ようだ
first_relatable.meaning: It seems that, It appears that, It looks like

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: Both convey hearsay, but differ in tone and formality. そうだ is used to directly pass on something you've heard, e.g. 明日は休みだそうだ ('I heard he has tomorrow off.') ということだ is more formal and often sounds more confident or declarative. It can also carry a nuance of explanation or conclusion, e.g. 明日は休みになるということだ ('So that means / They say we'll have tomorrow off.')

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: Both express hearsay, but with different tone and usage. んだって is very casual, often used in everyday conversation, and carries an explanatory tone due to んだ, e.g. 明日休みなんだって ('They said tomorrow's a day off, you know.') そうだ is more neutral and indirect, with no explanatory nuance, e.g. 明日休みだそうだ ('I heard tomorrow's a day off.')

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: Both can relay hearsay, but with different levels of certainty. とか adds a nuance of vagueness or uncertainty, e.g. 来月引っ越すとか ('I heard they might be moving next month, or something.') そうだ also conveys hearsay, but with less ambiguity, e.g. 来月引っ越すそうだ ('I heard they're moving next month.')

first_relatable.title: とか
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that… something like, They said ... or something

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: らしい ① and そうだ both convey information heard from another source, but with different nuances. らしい ① suggests hearsay with some degree of certainty, implying the speaker believes it to be true, e.g. 'Apparently it's (A)'. In contrast, そうだ is more neutral, simply meaning 'I heard (A).' or 'They say (A).'. They also connect differently to nouns and な-Adjectives, e.g. 大変らしい vs. 大変だそうだ (both meaning 'It seems difficult.').

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: Both ときいた and そうだ express hearsay, but with different nuances. ときいた means 'I heard (A).' and conveys information directly heard by the speaker, e.g., 高いときいた ('I heard it was expensive.'). In contrast, そうだ reports hearsay in a more abstract fashion, similar to 'They say (A).' in English.

second_relatable.title: そうだ
second_relatable.meaning: I heard that, It is said that

attributes.body: といわれている and そうだ both report something heard, but differ in nuance. といわれている is more general and formal, e.g. 'It is said that (A)'. On the other hand, そうだ often implies someone specific said it and is more casual, e.g., 雨が降るそうだ ('I heard it's going to rain.').
